class.name: PhysXParticleFluid3D
class.brief_description: A GPU position-based fluid simulated by the PhysX physics backend.
class.description: Fills a box-shaped region with fluid particles that are simulated on the GPU by PhysX 5 and collide with the rigid bodies in the same space. The particles are drawn as a [MultiMesh] of small spheres; [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override] applies to them. Particles can also be streamed in over time by enabling [member emitting], which turns the node into a faucet or hose: particles spawn near the node origin at [member emission_rate] per second with [member emission_velocity] (in node-local space) and, once [member particle_count] is reached, the oldest particles are recycled. This node only does anything when [member ProjectSettings.physics/3d/physics_engine] is set to [code]PhysX[/code], the engine was built with GPU support, and the machine has a usable CUDA device. Otherwise it is inert and emits a warning.

method.name: get_live_foam_count
method.description: Returns the number of diffuse (foam, spray, bubble) particles currently alive. Always [code]0[/code] unless [member foam_enabled] is set.

method.name: get_live_particle_count
method.description: Returns the number of particles currently simulated.

method.name: get_particle_positions
method.description: Returns the world-space position of every live particle, as read back from the GPU after the last physics step.

method.name: get_submersion
method.description: Returns the fraction (0 to 1) of the given world-space box currently filled with fluid, estimated from the number of particles inside it. A cheap probe for script-side buoyancy: PhysX PBD collides rigid bodies with the fluid but does not float or sink them by density, so apply your own buoyant force based on this value.

method.name: spawn
method.description: Fills [member spawn_region_size], centered on the node, with a jittered grid of particles spaced [member particle_size] apart (up to [member particle_count]). Replaces any particles already present. Called automatically on entering the tree when [member spawn_on_ready] is enabled.

members.member: How strongly particles clump together. Higher values give a more gel-like fluid.
Radius of the disc around the node origin that streamed particles spawn within, in meters. Only used while [member emitting].
Number of particles spawned per second while [member emitting].
Initial velocity given to streamed particles, in node-local space (it is rotated by the node's global transform). Its length is the spawn speed. Only used while [member emitting].
When enabled, the node continuously streams new particles from its origin, acting as a faucet or hose. Once [member particle_count] particles are live, the oldest are recycled to make room.
How strongly bubble-type foam particles (those below the surface) rise back up, from 0 to 1. Only used when [member foam_enabled] is set.

When enabled, the solver spawns diffuse particles — foam, spray and bubbles — wherever the fluid is agitated enough (splashes, streams hitting a pool, fast-moving crests). They do not affect the fluid. With [member surface_mesh] on they are drawn as their own coarse isosurface layer — a whiter, rougher froth that sits on the water and depth-sorts with it; otherwise they are drawn as a cloud of small spheres. Toggling this or changing [member foam_particle_count] rebuilds the particle buffer.
How long, in seconds, a diffuse particle lives before it disappears. Only used when [member foam_enabled] is set.
Maximum number of diffuse particles. Only used when [member foam_enabled] is set.

Froth clump scale, in meters, for the foam layer — independent of [member particle_size]. Larger values give chunkier sea-foam, smaller values a finer spray. [code]0[/code] means follow [member particle_size]. Only used when [member foam_enabled] is set; changing it while [member surface_mesh] is on rebuilds the foam extractor.
How agitated the fluid must be locally before diffuse particles spawn there. Lower values produce foam more readily. Only used when [member foam_enabled] is set.

Capacity of the particle buffer. For [method spawn] this is also limited by how many fit in [member spawn_region_size] at [member particle_size] spacing; for [member emitting] it is the point at which the oldest particles start being recycled.
Rest distance between neighboring particles, in meters. Also the diameter of the rendered spheres. Drives the fluid's rest density.
When enabled, [method spawn] runs automatically the first time the node enters the world outside the editor.
Size of the box, centered on the node, that [method spawn] fills with particles.

Only used when [member surface_mesh] is enabled. Anisotropy is PhysX computing a per-particle ellipsoid from each particle's neighbor distribution instead of treating every particle as a sphere: a particle deep in the fluid stays round, while one on the surface or in a thin sheet is flattened and aligned to that surface. Feeding those ellipsoids to the isosurface extractor gives sharper wave crests and thinner splash sheets, so the surface looks less like a cluster of blobs. The trade-off is that a fast-moving or isolated particle gets a strongly stretched ellipsoid that marching cubes can mesh as a thin spike, so this is off by default and best reserved for a settled pool. Leave it disabled while the fluid is actively emitting or splashing.

When enabled, PhysX marching-cubes a smooth triangle mesh from the particles on the GPU (position smoothing + [code]PxIsosurfaceExtractor[/code], plus optional [member surface_anisotropy]) and this node draws that instead of the sphere [MultiMesh]. Apply a water look with [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override] (transparency + refraction).
Strength of the force that minimizes the fluid's surface area, rounding off droplets and edges.
Resistance to flow. Higher values make the fluid thicker and slower, like honey.
Vorticity confinement. Re-injects swirling motion that the solver would otherwise damp out, keeping the fluid lively.
